title: The Association between Ground Floor Features and Public Open Space Face-To-Face Interactions: Evidence from Nantou Village, Shenzhen
research_question: Are spatial Ground Floor Features (GFFs) correlated to Public Open Space Face-To-Face Interaction Density (POSFTFID)? If so, which spatial GFFs and land uses are correlated to POSFTFID, to what extent, and which GFFs are strongly correlated with POSFTFID and with individual users of the POS that may potentially engage in face-to-face interactions?

participants.description: 602 interactors and 598 potential interactors observed in Nantou Village, Shenzhen, China. The statistical analysis was based on 292 buildings and their adjacent Public Open Spaces (POSs).
participants.recruitment: Observations were collected via video recording of people interacting or potentially interacting in public open spaces adjacent to buildings.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Ground floor features (GFFs) of 292 buildings overlooking main streets in Nantou Village, Shenzhen, including ground floor area, indoor visible space, presence of stairs, adjacent Public Open Space (POS) area, and land use. The study also considered derived metrics: degree of visibility (ratio of indoor visible space to total internal space) and degree of exposure (ratio of POS area to ground floor area).

measures.construct: Public Open Space Face-To-Face Interaction Density (POSFTFID)
measures.instrument: Density of georeferenced points representing observed human face-to-face interactions (interactors) and potential interactors (individuals standing or sitting alone) in the POS adjacent to each building, calculated as a ratio of observations to total m² of POS area.
Measured in m² from cartographic information and on-site mapping.
Measured in m² (internal degree of visibility) from cartographic information and on-site mapping.
Dichotomous variable (dummy) indicating presence or absence of stairs at the ground floor.
Measured in m² (buffer area) from cartographic information and on-site mapping.
Categorized as Residential, Religious, Retail, Restaurant/Food, Cultural, Public Service, Educational.
Ratio of indoor visible area (m²) to total ground floor area (m²).
Ratio of POS area to the ground floor area of each building.

mechanisms: Smaller Public Open Spaces (POS) adjacent to buildings, leading to shorter building façades and increased fragmentation of the street façade, are associated with higher face-to-face interaction density.
More visible indoor spaces at the ground floor enhance the perception of activity and 'eyes on the street', which fosters social interaction.
The presence of stairs at the ground floor provides opportunities for pausing, sitting, or waiting, thereby promoting social interaction.
Food-related land uses (restaurants/food shops) act as important attractors and gathering points, fostering social interaction.
implementation_implications: Urban design strategies and planning policies should aim to create fragmented street fronts with smaller adjacent Public Open Spaces to enhance human face-to-face interaction.
Design of ground floors should prioritize high visibility into indoor spaces to promote social interaction.
Incorporating stairs at the ground floor of buildings can foster social interaction.
Promoting restaurant and food-related land uses at the ground floor can enhance public social life and mental health conditions in contemporary cities.

limitations: The sample size for behavioural analysis (N = 1200) is relatively small, which may limit data accuracy and the application of more advanced statistical techniques.
Data collection period was limited (two weekend days), requiring a longer period with a balanced presence of working and non-working days to address potential bias.
The study is a single case study in China; future research should include different case studies from various regions for more robust and comparative findings.
Future studies should consider the third dimension (height) of buildings, rather than solely focusing on ground floor area, especially in high-density urban environments with grade-separation.

crossref_abstract: With face-to-face interaction proving beneficial for mental health, there is still a paucity of research on the correlation between ground floor features (GFFs), defined here as the features of the ground floor of buildings overlooking a street, and public open space face-to-face interaction density (POSFTFID), defined as the density of human face-to-face interactions in the public open space (POS) adjacent to each building. Is there a correlation between GFFs and POSFTFID? This study aims to answer this question gaining empirical evidence from a Chinese village in the city (ViC). Behavioural mapping and statistical analysis were employed and the following GFFs were tested: Ground floor area, indoor visible space, presence of stairs, POS adjacent area, and land use. Results show an association between POSFTFID and: (1) The area of the POS adjacent to each building, (2) the degree of visibility (ratio of indoor visible space to total internal space) of the ground floor, (3) the presence of stairs. Moreover, food appears to be an important attribute fostering social interaction. Results can provide insights on future implications in urban design strategies and planning policies aiming at enhancing mental health conditions in contemporary cities.
